text: Databases store and organize information so we can find it quickly. The most common type is the relational database, which keeps data in tables with rows and columns. To get information, we write queries, usually in a language called SQL. Before building a database, we design a data model that shows how the tables connect. Indexes help speed up searches, like the index at the back of a book. However, not all databases use tables. NoSQL databases store data in flexible forms, such as documents, and work well for large or changing data. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your needs.
